name: Bhangala (Sikkimese Corn Bread)
ingredients: Ghee or vegetable oil for frying
instructions: 1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cornmeal, salt, and optional chilies or coriander.
2. Gradually add warm water to the mixture, kneading gently until a firm, pliable dough forms.
3. Divide the dough into small, equal-sized balls and flatten them into thick, circular discs using your palms.
4. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan or tawa over medium heat and lightly grease it with ghee or oil.
5. Place the corn discs on the hot pan and cook until golden brown spots appear on both sides.
6. Serve hot, traditionally paired with local spicy chutneys or a warm vegetable stew.
description: Bhangala is a staple bread of the indigenous communities of Sikkim. Made primarily from local maize, it reflects the traditional agrarian lifestyle of the Himalayan region. It is a hearty, wholesome dish often consumed as a quick breakfast or a travel snack, celebrated for its simple preparation and earthy, nutty flavor.
